Subject: Acme Bank — Data residency & region pinning follow-up

Hi John,

Thanks again for carving out time today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Recap: You confirmed that Acme Bank needs PII processed and logged in the EU, with strict controls on cross-border replication and audit logs accessible to your security team.
- Primary ask: Can Redwood guarantee primary processing + long-term backups are stored in the EU for your production workloads, with a documented failover plan for DR?
- Next steps we committed to: 1) Provide a short technical note on region pinning and failover behavior, 2) Attach our SOC 2 summary and a region-pinning one-pager, 3) Schedule a follow-up with your security/procurement teams.

Immediate clarifications: 
1) Region pinning model: Redwood supports per-customer region pinning. You can designate a primary region (e.g., eu-west-1) for inference and for automated backups/snapshots.
2) Cross-region failover: We support configurable cross-region failover policies. By default we do NOT replicate backups cross-region unless configured for DR; cross-region replication is an opt-in for customers that want an additional RTO/RPO SLAs.
3) Logs & auditing: Control-plane audit logs and access logs can be retained in-region (EU) and exported to your logging stack. We can include a support note on retention windows and export options.
4) Encryption & key management: Data at rest and in transit is encrypted. We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for private deployments and Dedicated customers; for Hosted EU customers we offer EU-region KMS options.

Attachments: redwood-region-pinning-one-pager.pdf, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (attached).

I'll loop in Marissa who can provide the short tech note with specifics (RPO/RTO, backup retention, and the exact failover behavior). If useful, we can also produce a one-page diagram for legal/procurement.

Proposed follow-up: Tue 12 May, 09:00–09:30 CET to include security and procurement — does that work?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Aditya — thanks for the summary. A few clarifying questions from our security team before we loop in procurement: 

- When you say backups/snapshots are "stored in-region by default", what exactly is backed up? Model artifacts, KV caches, and request logs?
- If we opt into cross-region replication for DR, what is the RPO/RTO guarantee and how long are replicated backups retained?
- Are audit logs (who accessed what, when) available in the EU and exportable to our SIEM with no PII in the exported payloads?
- For hosted customers, can we use a customer-managed KMS with keys seeded in the EU region?

Also, any impact on latency or throughput if we enforce region pinning and strict in-region backups? Our app is latency-sensitive in our EU region.

Thanks — want to make sure we capture answers in writing for procurement.

John
Head of Cloud Security
Acme Bank

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: John Smith <john.smith@acmebank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example.com>
Date: Thu, 07 May 2026 08:15:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Acme Bank — Data residency & region pinning follow-up

John — good questions, copying answers below (keeping short bullets for procurement/security):

> On Wed, 06 May 2026 09:08:00 +0100, John Smith wrote:
> - When you say backups/snapshots are "stored in-region by default", what exactly is backed up? Model artifacts, KV caches, and request logs?

- Backups/snapshots: We snapshot model-serving state (model artifacts and weight files) and runtime filesystem state used for inference. We do NOT snapshot live KV caches used for low-latency generation. KV caches are ephemeral and rebuilt on warmup; critical state is in the model artifact and config.
- Request logs: By default request metadata (timestamps, request ids, token counts) is retained per your retention policy. Full request payloads (input text) are treated as customer data — retention and storage location follow your agreed policy. For strict EU-only retention we pin request payload storage to EU and do not replicate across regions.

> - If we opt into cross-region replication for DR, what is the RPO/RTO guarantee and how long are replicated backups retained?

- DR replication: Cross-region replication is opt-in. For Dedicated/Private customers we offer a DR add-on with SLA targets: typical RPO is <1 hour (snapshot-based) and RTO depends on instance warm-up but we target <2 hours for whole-environment failover. For Hosted customers we can provide a best-effort DR offering; for contractual guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments. Retention of replicated backups is configurable; commonly customers choose 30/90/365-day windows.

> - Are audit logs (who accessed what, when) available in the EU and exportable to our SIEM with no PII in the exported payloads?

- Audit logs: Yes. Control-plane audit logs (auth events, admin actions, deployment changes) and runtime access logs can be retained in-region (EU). Exports to SIEM are supported; we can redact PII at export time or provide a metadata-only export depending on your policy. We can supply a sample export schema for your SIEM team.

> - For hosted customers, can we use a customer-managed KMS with keys seeded in the EU region?

- KMS: For Hosted EU customers we support region-scoped customer-managed keys (via cloud KMS). For Dedicated/Private we support HSM/KMS integrations (customer-managed keys are strongly recommended for regulated workloads).

> - Any impact on latency/throughput if we enforce region pinning and strict in-region backups?

- Performance impact: None for inference latency if the serving region matches your user region. Backups run asynchronously and do not impact runtime latency. If you enable synchronous cross-region replication for strong RPO, that could add write-path latency for artifacts; we generally recommend async replication with snapshot schedules to avoid runtime impact.

Attaching the one-pager and SOC 2 summary again.

Next step: Aditya — can you re-propose the Tue 12 May slot and I'll make sure Security + Procurement are invited. Also we should provide the short DR spec (1 pager) and the SIEM export schema before the meeting.
